SHAUN ABRAHAMS AND NPA THE FARCE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What lies behind the deafening silence of the NPA on rising pressure for the reinstatement of charges against the President?

Unique Selling Point:
NPA DEEP THROAT
JOHAN BOOYSEN INTERVIEW – HIS LEGAL BATTLE IS PERSONALLY LINKED TO SHAUN ABRAHAMS.

Summary:
It’s been (another) bad yea for the NPA – not only have they had their offices burgled in what seems to be an inside job in recent weeks, but they’ve been roundly trounced for selective prosecutions, turning a blind eye to the transgressions at the SABC, SAA and ESKOM and having to withdraw baseless changes against Pravin Gordhan.

Further information:
Top ranking officials that have dared to investigate matters that will show up government for the farce that it has become have prosecuted and persecuted in high level attempts to have them removed from the positions and by default the investigations.

Some of the most experienced prosecutors have left and simmering discord has crippled those who must clean up the country. Now the opposition DA has the President for NPA boss Shaun Abrahams’ head. Only the president can get rid of his own appointee. But, having defended himself and vowing to never step down after the Gorhan Fiasco, Abrahams is deadly silent – and this more than two months after the Supreme court rules the decision to withdraw the 783 charges against the President was irrational – no action has been taken.

We approach constitutional, legal and political analysts to explain the rise and eminent fall of Shaun Abrahams. We will also ask Abrahams for an interview on how he sees the developments of since he’s taken up the position – in light of the Pravin Fiasco and recent calls for his resignation.

PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN TAKEN ON BY THE NPA AND CAME OUT VICTORIOUS:

JOHAN BOOYSEN’s Case directly linked to Shaun Abrahams.
- Abrahams re-instituted charges against Booysen after Booysen had the charges set aside in the High Court – winning his case with costs

GENERAL SHADRACK SIBIYA – Found NOT GUILTY in fraud case. Magistrate found that there was the prosecutor did not prove the State’s case. Prosecutor responded saying the instruction came from higher up - this is in the transcripts.

PRAVIN GORDHAN

IN THE MAJORITY OF THESE CASES THE SAME STATE ADVOCATES & INVESTIGATORS ARE INVOVLED


CASES THAT HAVE GONE NOWHERE:

JIBA – ON SPECIAL LEAVE, despite being scrapped from the Advocates Roll.

ZUMA CORRUPTION CHARGES

THOSHAN PANDAY

ABRAHAMS' ARGUMENT
He argues that it is not his decision which cases gets prosecuted - but all of this has happened under his watch. Further more he will say that he can only intervene when a matter is taken on review. In terms of Article 179 of (not sure what law - will get it straight before I shoot) he has to consult with the victim, the complainant and the prosecutor of the case before making a decision - in Jiba's case Abrahams did not consult the prosecutor (Ferreira or Booysen the complainant). So again a case of following the law when it suits him.



OTHER POSSIBLE INTERVIEWS - WE COULD GET SHADRACK SIBIYA, THE DA / GLYNIS BREYTENBACH... I'm OPEN TO SUGGESTIONS.


Case Study:
Johan Booysen FORMER HEAD OF HAWKS KZN
NPA DEEP THROAT

Dr. Mathews Phosa
Prof. IVOR CHIPKIN EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
Mr. Mavuso Msimang

Press Release:


NPA
It’s been yet another bad year for the NPA. Not only have they had their offices burgled in what appears to be an inside job, but they’ve been roundly
trounced for selective prosecutions. What lies behind the deafening silence of the NPA on the reinstatement of charges against the president?

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Corruption in the realm of state owned institutions and para-statals is crippling the economy. While South Africa is continuously burdened by billions of rands lost to fraud and corruption, implicated board members simply get a slap on the wrist.

Despite explosive media leaks, gruelling parliamentary inquiries and internal investigations that have found grounds for criminal prosecution – it doesn’t seem that anyone is going to jail soon.

LINK: The NPA stands accused of protecting the corrupt and the connected while persecuting others with selective prosecutions which brings the leadership of Shaun Abrahams into question.

VO: Advocate Abrahams has been at the helm of The National Prosecuting Authority for two years - Trade unionist Zwelinzima Vavi is not impressed by his term so far.

DEREK: //How do you rate Shaun Abrahams in that role?
VAVI: Zero – he has not proven all of our theories wrong – he has been there with this spate of corruption that runs into billions of rands that is being pillaged from state owned enterprises which are being collapsed – he has not even secured a trial, worst of all a conviction

VO: We spoke to a highly placed source within the NPA. For fear of retribution, the person has asked for their identity to be hidden. This is a verbatim transcript of what the source said – it is a visual representation and the voice of an actress.

DEEPTHROAT: in the history of the NPA I don’t think we’ve ever spent so much time fighting not to prosecute when there’s cases that we should do// we’re opposing matters, we’re supporting the accused in the matters – I don’t know who we are working for...

VO: Professor Ivor Chipkin is one of the academic authors of The Betrayal Of a Promise report – it details how South Africa is being stolen in the world of state capture.

IVOR: We’ve used the notion of a shadow state – // what you start seeing in South Africa // is the decision making shifting away from formal constitutional spaces, It might well be that the NPA is prosecuting or exercising it’s function – but it’s not clear under what basis or what criteria its using on who to prosecute. M4

VO: The alarm was sounded last year October, when the then Finance Minster Pravin Gordhan faced what many would call a selective prosecution.

UPSOUND ABRAHAMS…GORDHAN CHARGES

PRAVIN: We had the best lawyers in the country telling us there was no substance

VO: Then Three weeks later....

UPSOUND ABRAHAMS: WITHDRAW CHARGES

LINK: There is a perception that the on-going deterioration of the NPA, the HAWKS, the police services is part of a deliberate ploy to diminish accountability for grand corruption linked to the presidency.

VAVI: the state institutions have been domesticated – they have been hollowed out, and they no longer represent the mandate they were created for.

VO: Despite high-profile charges from corruption, racketeering to treason being laid by opposition parties and civil society organisations, these cases don’t appear to be making it to court.

Luvuyo Mfaku is the spokesperson for the NPA.

LEVUYO: They are investigation with the police. We can’t do that investigate.

VO: Mfaku insists the NPA’s powers are limited.

LEVUYO: //we prosecute on the basis of complete investigation and no one can say the NPA is sitting with a docket where investigation is complete and they are not prosecuting.

VO: But some would argue the 783 Corruptions Charges against the President is one such docket.

It’s been a year since the Gauteng High Court ruled that the decision to withdraw the criminal charges against President Zuma - was irrational, and that the President “should face the charges as outlined in the indictment.”

VAVI: Any where else in a normal circumstances – President JZ would have long been put on trial and face the 783 charges, it wont happen because there is no NPA to do that

MFESANE: the problem unfortunately is far broader than simply prosecute the president – it speaks to the democratic dispensation that has been compromised.

VO: Criminal Law lecturer Mfesane Siboto says it would appear that not everyone is equal before the law.

MFESANE: if you look at this conglomerate of evidence // against the president which the national director of public prosecution does not seem to have an appetite to prosecute - over and above that he goes as far as wanting to appeal the decision of the high court.

VO: The NPA is taking the ruling to the Supreme Court of Appeal.

DEREK: Why doesn’t Advocate Abrahim allow the courts to settle the matter once and for all and give Jacob Zuma an opportunity to exonerate himself?
LEVUYO: The matter is before court. It’s coming up in September, we would have clarity on the matter, but we cannot circumvent due processes that are prescribed legislation and when… when it’s the president, we say now jungle justice must apply?
DEREK: I’m not saying jungle justice.//the High Court said the case must go ahead. Why not just accept that?
LEVUYO: We… we… there are legal issues and issues and issues that impact on the powers of the NPA. That must be clarified. //

VO: Mfaku is referring to confusion around procedural matters, and insists the NPA does not protect the accused.

But Siboto says it seems the NPA is wasting time – the Supreme Court of Appeal has already dealt with and ruled on a similar case.

MFESANE: They’ve made a pronouncement on that already// As to why we are going to the same court and asking the exact same question – baffles the mind – you cannot help but conclude there is a certainly deliberate attempt to delay this matter.

VAVI: we have arrived in a banana republic –// people act with impunity – nobody comes any where close to saying we have to account for what we have done to society.

VO: But Mfaku claims that the NPA is preforming better than ever.

LEVUYO: // Let me remind you, since Advocate Abrahams took office two years, exactly two years now. He has achieved an unprecedented conviction rate. // This year it’s 94.1.

VO: Chipkin says it’s all relative to the cases they choose to prosecute.

IVOR: we have some statistical evidence and what we definitely see the number of high-profile or politically connected people being prosecuted by the NPA has dropped sharply.

VO: And it seems the NPA are instead targeting the very people challenging and investigating corruption.

BOOYSEN: /I have no doubt in my mind that I have been a victim of selective prosecution.

VO: Former KZN Hawks Boss Johan Booysen officially retired in February. He is still challenging racketeering charges brought against him five years ago, these are related to the so-called Cato Manor Organised Crime Death Squad.

DEREK: Why do you thin the NPA is being selective?
BOOYSEN: you only have to look at the people who are the subjects of the investigations that I conducted while I was still part of the HAWKS. Those family members of the state president, Edward Zuma – Edward zuma is the silent partner of one of the businessman I had been investigating. The nephew of the state president, Mzobe is actually a registered partner of the businessman I was investigating – so you don’t need to be rocket scientist to figure that one out.

VO: So it seems the president’s men and his relatives are off limits. A lesson a number of crime fighters have had to learn says Booysen.

BOOYSEN: there are a number of people who seems to have the temerity to investigate corruption within the government they very soon become the subject of investigations, they are suspended, they are side-lined, they are prosecuted just to neutralise them.

VO: Former HAWKS Boss - Anwa Dramat; Former General Shadrack Sibiya, Former NPA Head Mxolisi Nxasana, IPID’s Robert McBride and former NPA prosecutor Glynnis Breytenbach all claim to have been targeted in NPA prosecutions.

Yet the SABC, PRASA, SAA and Eskom that have been embroiled in corruption to the tune of billions of rands - go years without prosecution.

IVOR: I’m sure the court processes obviously their evidence need to meet those legal standards, but there is masses and masses of prima facie evidence //

DEEPTHROAT: There is no vigour// from any of the organisations to tackle the information which is lying on the table, it’s lying on a platter. The media get it.

VO: The NPA say, the evidence in the public domain is not sufficient for prosecution.

DEREK: It’s public knowledge the amounts involved, the alleged corruption that is taking place. Why do you need much more evidence?
LUVUYO: //We cannot as an institution prosecute on the basis of a forensic report by either a private company or the Public Protector or SIU. Those reports must be subjected to a thorough criminal investigation by the police.

VO: In 2016, the then Public Protector Thuli Madonsela released her 355 page State Capture Report complete with damning supporting evidence. It has taken the NPA’S specialised commercial crime prosecutors eight months to decided that there is indeed a basis for criminal investigation.

VAVI: only now they are saying they are reviewing that they will act – they can’t act because // they are serving the interests of President zuma and the cronies that are around him.

LINK: While it’s enshrined in the constitution that the prosecuting authority carries out it functions without fear, favour or prejudice there are some within the NPA who say it’s not all that clear cut.

DEEPTHROAT: The feeling is that, or a very strong belief rather is that the political masters are puling the strings at the NPA //

VO: Sibioto confirms this is dangerous territory.

MFESANE: // – the way the constitution was crafted it was in such a way was that the authority of the NPA should be completely free of politics – and at the root of that principle is the concept of democracy and the rule of law – which can only be brought into realisation if they are independent.

VO: Vavi believes Shaun Abrahams is far from independent.

VAVI: I liken him with those type of monkeys you put a massive chain around his neck and you put them as a pet around your house for children to throw peanuts to // I think that is what he represents – nothing else – captured, shamefully captured.

MFAKU: //The NPA is not captured.//There’s a notion that because the President is an appointing authority and therefore the person appointed by him will not exercise his responsibility without fear, favour or prejudice.

VO: But Chipkin believes while there are delays in state entity cases, it opens the door for more corruption and the continued looting of state coffers.

IVOR: The brazenness of some of the operations, // they are not even trying to cover their tracks very much // If the NPA if there were prosecuting, if there were a sense that you can’t get away with this kind of thing I think a lot less of it would be happening

VAVI: A signal had been sent to the authorities that we have our man now in the highest office of the prosecution // what a waste, what a betrayal of the dream that Nelson Mandela promised all of us about.


PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Last year, the high court ruled that President Zuma should face the infamous 783 corruption charges – so what’s the delay?

VAVI: the state institutions have been domesticated

PROMO 2
VO: With allegations of selective prosecutions – there are questions around National Prosecuting Authority head, Advocate Shaun Abraham’s leadership & independence.

VAVI: they are serving the interests of President zuma and the cronies that are around him.

PROMO3
VO: The NPA stands accused of protecting the corrupt and the connected while persecuting others with selective prosecutions - has the NPA been captured?

The media get it. VO: The NPA say, the evidence in the public domain is not sufficient for prosecution. DEREK: It’s public knowledge the amounts involved, the alleged corruption that is taking place. Why do you need much more evidence? LUVUYO: //We cannot as an institution prosecute on the basis of a forensic report by either a private company or the Public Protector or SIU. Those reports must be subjected to a thorough criminal investigation by the police. VO: In 2016, the then Public Protector Thuli Madonsela released her 355 page State Capture Report complete with damning supporting evidence. It has taken the NPA’S specialised commercial crime prosecutors eight months to decided that there is indeed a basis for criminal investigation. VAVI: only now they are saying they are reviewing that they will act – they can’t act because // they are serving the interests of President zuma and the cronies that are around him. LINK: While it’s enshrined in the constitution that the prosecuting authority carries out it functions without fear, favour or prejudice there are some within the NPA who say it’s not all that clear cut. DEEPTHROAT: The feeling is that, or a very strong belief rather is that the political masters are puling the strings at the NPA // VO: Sibioto confirms this is dangerous territory. MFESANE: // – the way the constitution was crafted it was in such a way was that the authority of the NPA should be completely free of politics – and at the root of that principle is the concept of democracy and the rule of law – which can only be brought into realisation if they are independent. VO: Vavi believes Shaun Abrahams is far from independent. VAVI: I liken him with those type of monkeys you put a massive chain around his neck and you put them as a pet around your house for children to throw peanuts to // I think that is what he represents – nothing else – captured, shamefully captured. MFAKU: //The NPA is not captured.//There’s a notion that because the President is an appointing authority and therefore the person appointed by him will not exercise his responsibility without fear, favour or prejudice. VO: But Chipkin believes while there are delays in state entity cases, it opens the door for more corruption and the continued looting of state coffers. IVOR: The brazenness of some of the operations, // they are not even trying to cover their tracks very much // If the NPA if there were prosecuting, if there were a sense that you can’t get away with this kind of thing I think a lot less of it would be happening VAVI: A signal had been sent to the authorities that we have our man now in the highest office of the prosecution // what a waste, what a betrayal of the dream that Nelson Mandela promised all of us about. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Last year, the high court ruled that President Zuma should face the infamous 783 corruption charges – so what’s the delay? VAVI: the state institutions have been domesticated PROMO 2 VO: With allegations of selective prosecutions – there are questions around National Prosecuting Authority head, Advocate Shaun Abraham’s leadership & independence. VAVI: they are serving the interests of President zuma and the cronies that are around him. PROMO3 VO: The NPA stands accused of protecting the corrupt and the connected while persecuting others with selective prosecutions - has the NPA been captured? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What lies behind the deafening silence of the NPA on rising pressure for the reinstatement of charges against the President?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: NPA DEEP THROAT JOHAN BOOYSEN INTERVIEW – HIS LEGAL BATTLE IS PERSONALLY LINKED TO SHAUN ABRAHAMS.
metadata.Summary: It’s been (another) bad yea for the NPA – not only have they had their offices burgled in what seems to be an inside job in recent weeks, but they’ve been roundly trounced for selective prosecutions, turning a blind eye to the transgressions at the SABC, SAA and ESKOM and having to withdraw baseless changes against Pravin Gordhan.
metadata.Further information: Top ranking officials that have dared to investigate matters that will show up government for the farce that it has become have prosecuted and persecuted in high level attempts to have them removed from the positions and by default the investigations. Some of the most experienced prosecutors have left and simmering discord has crippled those who must clean up the country. Now the opposition DA has the President for NPA boss Shaun Abrahams’ head. Only the president can get rid of his own appointee. But, having defended himself and vowing to never step down after the Gorhan Fiasco, Abrahams is deadly silent – and this more than two months after the Supreme court rules the decision to withdraw the 783 charges against the President was irrational – no action has been taken. We approach constitutional, legal and political analysts to explain the rise and eminent fall of Shaun Abrahams. We will also ask Abrahams for an interview on how he sees the developments of since he’s taken up the position – in light of the Pravin Fiasco and recent calls for his resignation. PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN TAKEN ON BY THE NPA AND CAME OUT VICTORIOUS: JOHAN BOOYSEN’s Case directly linked to Shaun Abrahams. - Abrahams re-instituted charges against Booysen after Booysen had the charges set aside in the High Court – winning his case with costs GENERAL SHADRACK SIBIYA – Found NOT GUILTY in fraud case. Magistrate found that there was the prosecutor did not prove the State’s case. Prosecutor responded saying the instruction came from higher up - this is in the transcripts. PRAVIN GORDHAN IN THE MAJORITY OF THESE CASES THE SAME STATE ADVOCATES & INVESTIGATORS ARE INVOVLED CASES THAT HAVE GONE NOWHERE: JIBA – ON SPECIAL LEAVE, despite being scrapped from the Advocates Roll. ZUMA CORRUPTION CHARGES THOSHAN PANDAY ABRAHAMS' ARGUMENT He argues that it is not his decision which cases gets prosecuted - but all of this has happened under his watch. Further more he will say that he can only intervene when a matter is taken on review. In terms of Article 179 of (not sure what law - will get it straight before I shoot) he has to consult with the victim, the complainant and the prosecutor of the case before making a decision - in Jiba's case Abrahams did not consult the prosecutor (Ferreira or Booysen the complainant). So again a case of following the law when it suits him. OTHER POSSIBLE INTERVIEWS - WE COULD GET SHADRACK SIBIYA, THE DA / GLYNIS BREYTENBACH... I'm OPEN TO SUGGESTIONS.
